note: letters-only or digits-only request over a range holding no such character looped forever; two scan-and-throw blocks added; the -12 are the numbers-to-digits rename and re-wraps, so addition-only

guard halved only a MIN_VALUE denominator, so MIN_VALUE over an even negative denominator threw overflow; clause replaced by a denominator-evenness test and if by while, a replacement rather than an added clause
matching but out-of-range GMT offset (hours >= 24 or minutes >= 60) reached the GmtTimeZone constructor, which threw instead of the documented null; range guard added, addition-only
null value starting a record printed as an empty unquoted field, leaving an empty line that ignoreEmptyLines drops; new branch quotes it in minimal mode, original append kept as else-branch
Character.digit(c, 16) accepts non-ASCII Unicode digits and fullwidth letters, so hexDigitToInt converted characters that are not hex digits; fix validates with CharUtils.isHex; misuse of a JDK API

reflection calls (isAnonymousClass, getDeclaringClass chain) throw NoClassDefFoundError when the enclosing class is missing; original block wrapped in try/catch with a name-based fallback; the -1 only drops final

WildcardTypeImpl broke the equals/hashCode contract with JDK wildcards; hashCode rewritten to the JDK formula over the bounds equals compares, and the constructor's empty default upper bound replaced by Object
escaping path left the quote character unescaped, so a value containing it did not round-trip; quoteSet && c == quote added to the existing escape condition in both printWithEscapes overloads
createNumber accepted a leading space or control character on the float and double paths, whose JDK parsers trim, unlike the integral ones; leading-character guard added, addition-only
negative (proleptic BC) week year reached digit rules that cannot render a sign; sign branch added to appendTo(int), calendar overload routed through it with the original rule call kept
hand-written NaN check and comparison did not order -0.0 below 0.0 as Math.max/min do; comparison approach replaced by Math.max/min in all four float and double array methods
CEILING rounded a value already on the field boundary up to the next unit; the existing round-up condition gained originalMillis != val.getTimeInMillis() for CEILING
int cross products u*v' and u'*v were overflow-checked one by one, throwing although the result fits an int; rewritten in long with one final narrowing, the add/sub helpers deleted
with a multi-character delimiter, a value ending in a prefix of it merged with the following delimiter on read; new helper and else-if branch force quoting, addition-only
isDelimiter consumes a multi-character delimiter's tail as a side effect but ran twice per character, the second call seeing an advanced reader; result now computed once and remembered

unnamed package unhandled: null Class.getPackage() gave NPE and an empty package name a leading separator; guards added in all four methods, originals kept as ternary else-branches (requireNonNull wrapper redundant)
whitespace at the end of the pattern left seekNonWs at the end and charAt then threw; bounds check with break added after it, the -5 are re-wrapped throw statements
contains(CharRange) with a negated argument covered only the full-range case, missing negated ranges whose low or high part is empty; three branches added before the existing return, addition-only
negative csStart started the scan at a negative index and charAt threw; loop start clamped with Math.max(csStart, 0), an unconditional transform under rule 2, so a wrong value rather than an addition
reused delimiterBuf kept characters from an earlier read, so delimiter matching could use stale data; buffer now cleared at the start of each token, a stale-state fault; +2 includes the import
int mask stored in a long field was sign-extended, so a mask with bit 31 set gained 32 high bits; Integer.toUnsignedLong substituted, shiftCount computed from the widened mask
padded text was passed to Formatter.format as the format string, so a % in it was parsed as a specifier; fix formats it through SIMPLEST_FORMAT; misuse of the Formatter API
pattern compiled without DOTALL, so . did not match line terminators and words in multi-line input were not found; Pattern.DOTALL added; misuse of the java.util.regex API

Duration.toMillis() overflow threw ArithmeticException out of toMillisInt, documented to clamp; call wrapped in try/catch saturating to MIN/MAX, and StopWatch.formatSplitTime rerouted through toMillisInt, a modified line, so not addition-only
a varargs method matched calls passing fewer arguments than its fixed parameters; the existing isVarArgs() condition gained a length clause
bulk read(char[], int, int) advanced position but never added to bytesRead, so byte tracking undercounted; helper and update added, the -2 are the re-wrapped read() condition

endIndexExclusive of Integer.MIN_VALUE made min(...) - 1 wrap to MAX_VALUE and index past the array; max0 clamp wraps the expression in all nine overloads, an unconditional transform, so a wrong value
a unicode escape whose four characters began with + or - was parsed by Integer.parseInt, which accepts a sign, instead of being rejected; sign check added before the parse, addition-only
off-by-one boundary test: startPos > endLimit let startPos == endLimit through, where an empty search string returned an index past the end; relational operator > replaced by >=
deprecated getStopTime dereferenced a null stop instant, throwing NPE; null guard added as a ternary keeping the original call chain as its true branch
print synchronized on the publicly reachable format instance rather than the existing writeLock; critical section moved into synchronized (writeLock); lock identity and thread safety under rule 6
equals and hashCode ignored the maxRows field; the existing equals conjunction gained maxRows == other.maxRows and the hash gained maxRows, the rest is re-wrapping
